classification.difficultyReason: Read horizontal and vertical extents from supplied graphs, distinguishing included bounds, limiting values and singleton sets.

inlines.text: State the domain and range of the following.

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 1 column 1, printed question 7
spec.description: Increasing S-shaped curve through the axes' intersection, with a horizontal-looking tangent there and continuation arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Both horizontal and vertical projections are unbounded. No equation or numerical scale is supplied; Bézier controls reconstruct the qualitative source shape only.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied graph is visible; domain and range responses remain in answers.

answer.worked:
The graph extends indefinitely left and right, and down and up.
$$\begin{align*}D&=(-\infty,\infty)\\R&=(-\infty,\infty)\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 1 column 2, printed question 8
spec.description: Upward-opening parabola with arrowed arms, a filled vertex at (3,1), and dashed projections to both labelled axes.
spec.mathematics: The included minimum is y=1 at x=3. Both arms continue upward. No equation or curvature coefficient is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The vertex, guides and numerical labels are permanent givens; responses remain hidden with answers.

answer.worked:
The parabola extends indefinitely left and right. Its minimum value is $1$, which is included.
$$\begin{align*}D&=(-\infty,\infty)\\R&=[1,\infty)\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 2 column 1, printed question 9
spec.description: Finite wave from a filled point at (-2π,0), through a crest, the origin and a trough, to a filled point at (2π,0).
spec.mathematics: The horizontal endpoints are -2π and 2π; the attained vertical extrema are 1 and -1. There are no curve arrows. The source supplies no equation or exact horizontal locations for the extrema; unlabelled Bézier controls are schematic.
spec.answerVisibility: Endpoint markers and axis values remain visible; no domain or range annotation is placed on the graph.

answer.worked:
Both horizontal endpoints are included. The graph reaches both its minimum $-1$ and maximum $1$.
$$\begin{align*}D&=[-2\pi,2\pi]\\R&=[-1,1]\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 2 column 2, printed question 10
spec.description: Increasing exponential-shaped curve through (0,1), approaching the x-axis from above on the left and rising on the right, with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: The curve remains strictly above y=0 and extends over every x-value. No exponential base or equation is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source curve and y-intercept label are supplied.

answer.worked:
The curve extends over every $x$-value. It approaches $y=0$ without reaching it and rises without bound.
$$\begin{align*}D&=(-\infty,\infty)\\R&=(0,\infty)\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 3 column 1, printed question 11
spec.description: Downward-opening parabola symmetric about the y-axis, with maximum (0,1) and downward arrows on both arms.
spec.mathematics: The maximum height 1 is attained. The x-intercepts are unlabelled, and no equation is asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied maximum-height label is visible; no additional vertex marker or answer annotation is added.

answer.worked:
The parabola extends indefinitely left and right. Its maximum value is $1$, which is included.
$$\begin{align*}D&=(-\infty,\infty)\\R&=(-\infty,1]\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 3 column 2, printed question 12
spec.description: Increasing concave-down curve to the right of the dashed asymptote x=1, crossing the x-axis at 2, with lower and upper-right continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: The vertical asymptote is excluded; the curve continues without vertical bound in either direction. No logarithmic equation or base is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: The asymptote and intercept labels are question givens; responses are separate.

answer.worked:
The curve lies strictly to the right of $x=1$. It extends indefinitely downward and upward.
$$\begin{align*}D&=(1,\infty)\\R&=(-\infty,\infty)\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 4 column 1, printed question 13
spec.description: Increasing concave-down curve beginning at the origin and continuing into the first quadrant with an upper-right arrow.
spec.mathematics: The starting point is included. Both projections begin at zero and continue positively without bound. No equation or scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: No point marker, numerical label or answer annotation is added.

answer.worked:
The curve starts at the included origin and continues rightward and upward.
$$\begin{align*}D&=[0,\infty)\\R&=[0,\infty)\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 4 column 2, printed question 14
spec.description: Upper semicircle centred at the axes' intersection, with endpoints at x=-3 and x=3 and maximum y=3.
spec.mathematics: The semicircle has radius 3 and includes its endpoints. Equal x- and y-units preserve the circular geometry.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source axis labels and the complete unfilled arc are visible.

answer.worked:
The semicircle includes both endpoints and reaches height $3$.
$$\begin{align*}D&=[-3,3]\\R&=[0,3]\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 5 column 1, printed question 15
spec.description: Closed horizontal ellipse centred at the origin, meeting the axes at x=±3 and y=±2.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal and vertical semiaxes are 3 and 2. All extrema are included; the relation need not be a function of x.
spec.answerVisibility: No centre marker, fill, continuation arrow or answer annotation is added.

answer.worked:
The ellipse reaches $x=-3$ and $x=3$, and $y=-2$ and $y=2$. All four bounds are included.
$$\begin{align*}D&=[-3,3]\\R&=[-2,2]\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 5 column 2, printed question 16
spec.description: Closed circle tangent to the y-axis at y=1, with top y=3, bottom y=-1, rightmost extent x=4, x-axis labels 2 and 4, and horizontal guides to the vertical extrema.
spec.mathematics: The supplied extrema determine centre (2,1) and radius 2 for construction. The centre is not marked or labelled. Equal x- and y-units retain the circle; the two x-intercepts remain unlabelled.
spec.answerVisibility: All source labels and guides remain visible; derived centre and radius are not printed.

answer.worked:
The circle extends horizontally from $0$ to $4$ and vertically from $-1$ to $3$, including all bounds.
$$\begin{align*}D&=[0,4]\\R&=[-1,3]\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 6 column 1, printed question 17
spec.description: Vertical line through x=2, with continuation arrows above and below.
spec.mathematics: Every point has x=2, while y is unrestricted. The line is a relation, not a function of x.
spec.answerVisibility: The source x-axis value is visible; the singleton-domain response is not printed.

answer.worked:
Every point has $x=2$, while $y$ can be any real number.
$$\begin{align*}D&=\{2\}\\R&=(-\infty,\infty)\end{align*}$$

spec.sourceRegion: Left column, graph grid row 6 column 2, printed question 18
spec.description: Horizontal line through y=-1, with continuation arrows to the left and right.
spec.mathematics: Every real x-value occurs, and every point has y=-1.
spec.answerVisibility: The source y-axis value is visible; the singleton-range response remains in answers.

answer.worked:
The line covers every $x$-value and has the single $y$-value $-1$.
$$\begin{align*}D&=(-\infty,\infty)\\R&=\{-1\}\end{align*}$$
